c.tagline: Where two continents share a single skyline.

avoid.reason: Tourist scams (the "friendly local"/rigged bar bill, shoeshine drop, overpriced rugs), pickpocketing in Sultanahmet and on Istiklal/Taksim; caution in some areas at night

hood_desc: The historic heart of old Istanbul, home to the Hagia Sophia, Blue Mosque and Topkapi Palace, with narrow cobbled streets and countless carpet and souvenir shops. Ideal for first-time visitors who want major sights within walking distance.

A lively, cosmopolitan district centered on Istiklal Avenue and Taksim Square, packed with cafes, bars, galleries and nightlife. Suits travelers who want to be in the buzzing cultural and entertainment core of the modern city.
A trendy, laid-back neighborhood on the Asian side full of hip cafes, bars, bookshops and a famous produce market. Great for those seeking a more local, bohemian and less touristy vibe.

An upscale, energetic waterfront district with a busy market, seaside promenade, football culture and buzzing nightlife. Appeals to visitors wanting stylish restaurants and a youthful, upmarket atmosphere.
A stylish, artsy quarter by the Golden Horn with design boutiques, galleries, rooftop bars and waterfront views. Perfect for creative types drawn to a chic, revitalized industrial waterfront.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Istanbul at Sultanahmet

water.note: Officially potable but most locals and visitors use bottled water due to old plumbing and taste.

transit.pay: Buy an Istanbulkart from the yellow machines at stations, airports and major stops (small non-refundable card fee of a few US dollars), then top it up with cash or card — it covers metro, trams, ferries, buses and funiculars with cheap transfers. Contactless bank cards are also accepted at most readers, but at a higher per-ride fare. Single rides cost well under US$1 with the card.
transit.hours: Metro and trams run roughly 6am to midnight, with late-night service on some metro lines at weekends; night buses run overnight. Ferries run mainly in daytime.

landmarks: Hagia Sophia
A former Byzantine cathedral and Ottoman mosque whose massive dome and shifting religious history make it one of the world's most photographed interiors.
Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque)
Famous for its six minarets and cascading domes covered inside with thousands of blue Iznik tiles, facing Hagia Sophia across Sultanahmet Square.
Topkapı Palace
The opulent former residence of Ottoman sultans, prized for its courtyards, treasury, and sweeping views over the Bosphorus and Golden Horn.
Basilica Cistern
An eerie, cavernous 6th-century underground reservoir supported by hundreds of illuminated columns, including two famous Medusa-head bases.
Grand Bazaar
One of the world's oldest and largest covered markets, a maze of thousands of shops beneath ornate painted vaults.
Galata Tower
A medieval stone tower rising above the Golden Horn, offering a 360-degree panorama that is one of the classic Istanbul skyline shots.
Dolmabahçe Palace
A lavish 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, known for its crystal staircase, giant chandeliers, and European-style grandeur.
Süleymaniye Mosque
The grand 16th-century imperial mosque designed by architect Mimar Sinan, admired for its harmonious dome and hilltop views over the city.
Maiden's Tower
A small islet tower at the mouth of the Bosphorus wrapped in legend, forming an iconic silhouette especially at sunset.
Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar)
A fragrant 17th-century market of spices, sweets, and teas near the Golden Horn, beloved for its colorful stalls and historic L-shaped hall.

intl.to: Bucharest (Romania) - summer only, mid-June to mid-Oct
intl.op: TCDD / CFR Calatori (Bosfor Express through car)

train.note: International sleepers leave nightly from Halkali station on the European side (reachable by Marmaray suburban train); in Turkiye tickets are sold at Halkali and Sirkeci international ticket offices, not online. YHT high-speed trains to Ankara and Konya also call at Halkali, Bakirkoy and Sogutlucesme.

bus.note: International coaches use the big Esenler (Otogar) and Alibeykoy terminals - allow time for passport checks at the land borders. Many more Balkan, Caucasus and Middle East routes are run by smaller local firms; buy those at the otogar.

ferry.note: No scheduled international ferries sail from Istanbul - Black Sea passenger services to Ukraine remain suspended since 2022. IDO (ido.com.tr/en) and BUDO run domestic fast ferries across the Sea of Marmara; boats to the Greek islands leave from Aegean ports such as Cesme, Ayvalik and Bodrum instead.

half.name: Princes' Islands (Büyükada)
half.blurb: Car-free islands with pine woods, old mansions and horse-drawn carriage tradition just offshore.

half.name: Lake Sapanca
half.blurb: A tranquil lake ringed by green hills, popular for lakeside walks and fresh mountain air.

half.name: Şile
half.blurb: A Black Sea beach town with sandy shores, a lighthouse and a seaside castle.

half.name: Ağva
half.blurb: A quiet riverside village between two rivers, loved for boat rides and calm beaches.

full.name: Bursa
full.blurb: An early Ottoman capital known for grand mosques, thermal baths and Uludağ mountain.

full.name: Edirne
full.blurb: A former Ottoman capital home to the magnificent Selimiye Mosque near the Greek border.
